question:
Two masses of 1 kg and 2 kg were dropped from a height of 3.2 metres. Their respective velocities just before touching the ground will be:

(Assume acceleration due to gravity g = 10 m/s²)
solution:
The correct answer is __**8 m/s for both**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The velocities of objects falling freely under gravity are independent of their masses.
 
• Both the 1 kg and 2 kg masses will experience the same acceleration due to gravity (g = 10 m/s²).
 
• The velocity just before touching the ground is determined by the equation v = sqrt{2gh}, where g is the acceleration due to gravity and h is the height from which the object is dropped.
 
• Using the formula v = sqrt{2 times 10 times 3.2} = sqrt{64} = 8 {m/s}, both masses will have the same velocity just before hitting the ground.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity:**

 
 
• Gravity is a fundamental force that attracts objects towards the center of the Earth.
 
• The value of acceleration due to gravity near Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s² but is commonly approximated as 10 m/s² for simplicity in calculations.
 
• The value of gravity can vary depending on location, altitude, and Earth's irregular shape.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall:**
 
 
• When an object is dropped, and the only force acting on it is gravity, it is said to be in free fall.
 
• Objects in free fall accelerate at a constant rate due to gravity, regardless of their mass.
 
 
 
• **Formula for Velocity in Free Fall:**
 
 
• The velocity of an object just before hitting the ground can be found using the formula v = sqrt{2gh}, where g is the gravitational acceleration and h is the height.
 
• This equation assumes there is no air resistance.
 
 
 
• **Mass and Gravity:**
 
 
• In the absence of air resistance, all objects fall at the same rate regardless of their mass. This was famously demonstrated by Galileo.
